entries.source: MISO/SPP JOA (Midwest and South footprints exchange power only over the RDT contract path across SPP); 2025 diagnostic probe measured the shared-bus bypass at 1,255 MW summer mean / 7.7 TWh-yr vs an RDT S->N binding 13 h/yr

entries.name: miso_rdt_tcdc (RDT 92% default derate + $40/$500 TCDC tiers)
entries.where: constants.MISO_RDT_* via transmission.apply_miso_rdt_tcdc; priced one-way tiers (TransferLink.flow_cost)
entries.source: 2024 MISO SOM §III.B (92% default derate; two-step TCDC $40 at the modeled limit, $500 from 102%); MISO/SPP JOA Attach. A (3,000 N->S / 2,500 S->N contract limits)
entries.note: deliberately conservative: the 92% DEFAULT derate is used, not the deeper condition-driven operator derates (utilization averaged 84% of contract when binding in 2024, SOM §II.E) — no published hourly derate series, so binding-hour congestion under-shoots rather than fitting a haircut; re-derives only when MISO publishes new TCDC/derate parameters (rule 23)

entries.name: miso_rpe_pricing (RPE $200 additive on RDT violation tiers)
entries.where: constants.MISO_RPE_DEMAND_VALUE via transmission.apply_miso_rdt_tcdc (rpe_pricing=True); adds to the two violation tiers' TransferLink.flow_cost only
entries.source: 2024 MISO SOM §II.E ('MISO enforces STR requirements in its two subregions by enforcing reserve procurement enhancement (RPE) constraints over the RDT') + §III.B (single $200/MWh demand value; RDT+RPE 'apply additively' in real violations — measured $700 spreads, small violations overpriced by $200); IMM Summer-2025 quarterly ($41M RDT+RPE congestion, +121% YoY)
entries.note: deliberately conservative: the RPE's STR-scarcity binding channel (binds with NO RDT violation when importing-subregion STR is limited — the quarterly's 'RPE Only' category) is unrepresented because the LP carries no STR product, so separation under-shoots; the IMM's cap-at-$500 recommendation was not implemented in-window — date-gate the re-anchor if MISO adopts it (rule 23)

entries.name: unit_outage_short_windows (< 5-day baseload-coal CEMS windows)
entries.where: data/raw/campd-unit-outages-short-{ISO}.csv via outages.unit_outage_short_derate_factors (applied next to the >= 5-day parent overlay; disjoint by construction)
entries.source: per-unit EPA CAMPD hourly gross generation (scripts/derive_campd_unit_outages.py --short-windows); identification guards: coal-only detector + unit annual CF >= 0.55 (the partial-outage detector's baseload constant) + the revealed-availability in-merit filter (derive_campd_outages.filter_revealed_outages; the full-stop override cannot engage below the 5-day cap)
entries.note: the >= 5-day duration floor makes event-coincident short forced outages invisible (MISO Jul 28-29 2025: ~2.8 GW coal offline at the peak block beyond the overlay; docs/DIAGNOSIS-miso-july2025-lmp-2026-07.md); CT/CC event unavailability stays unmodeled pending a max-gen-event registry intake (no identification without it)

entries.name: class_aware_fuel_price_fallback (same-class F923 donor pools)
entries.where: data.fuel._NearbyFuelPrices same-class tier (state -> zone -> class-blind fuel-group fallback); donor plants classified by capacity-dominant model class within the fuel group
entries.source: EIA-923 Schedule-5 delivered fuel costs (the same F923 parquet the fallback already reads), re-pooled by plant class; measured basis: MISO 2024 CT filers $4.13/MMBtu cap-wtd vs CC $2.57 while the quantity-weighted class-blind pool is CC-burn-dominated (~$2.6)
entries.note: the class-blind donor priced the ~33% of non-filing CT capacity ~$16-20/MWh below its measured class cost, feeding the 2024 CT_PEAKER economic over-run at PRB's expense and July-2025's too-cheap North margin (docs/DIAGNOSIS-miso-july2025-lmp-2026-07.md §6, lane 1(b))

entries.name: coal_warm_committed (warm-boiler committed-band exemption)
entries.where: model.commitment.compute_monthly_markup warm-boiler branch; gated per plant on must_run_pct > 0 (CAMPD thermal-tranche artifact)
entries.source: dispatch forensics on the miso-58 2023 replay (on/off LMP crossings: COAL_PRB committed $34.6 vs ~$26 static F923 SRMC, COAL_BIT $43.8 vs ~$29-31, mustrun bands online 84-98% of the same hours) + MISO IMM measured conduct (som-competitive-conduct: offers AT cost, system price-cost markup +3.0%/-2.5% — self-committed units recover start costs outside the energy offer)
entries.note: removes a fabricated cold-start premium, adds no tunable; reverts only if the fleet's measured must-run floors disappear (rule 23: rides the thermal-tranche artifact refresh)

entries.name: MISO COAL SOM near-cost offer floor
entries.where: pipeline/backcast_config.py _MISO_OFFER_CURVE COAL_* entries (committed/econ_low = 1.00) + calibration_flags coal_prb/bit_passthrough_sigmoid=False, coal_prb_passthrough_tiered=False
entries.source: the MISO IMM's measured conduct statistics (datatype som-competitive-conduct; freeze test tests/test_curate_som_competitive_conduct.py): system price-cost mark-up +3.0% (2023) / -2.5% (2024) — offers AT reference levels ~= SRMC — and output gap 'effectively de minimis' (0.1%/0.06% of load; 2025 quarterlies 22-71 MW/hr). The measured discount depth is ~none, so every MISO coal tranche above must-run bids full measured F923 delivered SRMC: the gas-keyed passthrough sigmoid MECHANISM is replaced for MISO (not re-parameterized) and the sub-1.0 band multipliers raised to exactly 1.00 — a zero-discount anchor, no fitted value (n_scalars 0). Self-commitment (SOM Table 7: must-run status on 56%/53% of regulated coal starts) remains represented by the per-plant fuel-free _mustrun band (coal_mustrun_per_plant, CAMPD thermal_tranches_MISO.csv), one mechanism per phenomenon (rule 19). Adjudication record: docs/handoffs/miso-coal-offer-som-redesign-2026-07.md. Re-derive trigger: the 2025 MISO SOM publication (rule 23).

entries.name: gas_daily_shape[MISO]
entries.where: backcast_config.py gas_daily_shape (MISO added 2026-07-09); factors from data/raw/gas-prices/henry_hub_daily.csv via fuel.gas_daily_shape_factors
entries.source: measured Henry Hub daily spot (EIA RNGWHHD), normalized to each month's own daily mean (mean-preserving, so the monthly EIA-923 plant-level delivered gas level and the annual mix are unchanged); no fitted value — the factors ARE the data. Closes the miso-50 rule-23 granularity caveat's free-data leg; the daily basin-basis leg (Chicago Citygate daily) remains the open paywalled ask.

entries.name: hydro 2025 completeness (backfill 2024 + EIA-930 monthly repin)

governance.attested_by: miso-65 outage-regen 2026-07-14: the miso-64 KEEPER recipe replayed VERBATIM (scripts/probes/_miso65_outage_regen.py — the miso-62 meta.json strict RENAME/SKIP replay + miso_rpe_pricing + unit_outage_short_windows + class_aware_fuel_price_fallback, all kept armed) with ZERO flag or parameter changes. The only delta is the regenerated measured input campd-unit-outages-MISO.csv (commit 7b5c26fd): the committed >= 5-day unit-outage extract (PR #1820 vintage) did not reproduce from its own FROZEN deriver on the committed CAMPD unit-level parquets — re-running scripts/derive_campd_unit_outages.py --iso MISO --years 2023 2024 2025 (guards, constants and defaults untouched; the only deriver commit since #1820 is the purely-additive --short-windows mode) emits 1,655 windows the committed file lacked (2,924 -> 4,418 rows; +~1,550 GW-days in EACH of 2023/2024/2025), among them seven >= 5-day July-2025 North coal sustained full stops at span-CF < 0.002 (Ottumwa 1, Gibson 3, Labadie 2, Baldwin 2, Cayuga 1/2, Sioux 1) that the full-stop override keeps unconditionally. July North-coal outage coverage rises 2.75 -> 4.00 GW mean (2023 5.32 -> 7.03, 2024 4.63 -> 6.26); verified disjoint from the short-window companion file (0 same-unit overlaps). Lane 3 (docs/FINDING-miso-lane3-north-supply-2026-07.md): the stale extract left the model's July North coal shelf ~1.3-1.7 GW too deep in every backcast year — the phantom depth that kept the S->N corridor from separating.
governance.note: Lane 3 (North supply-curve depth / N-S separation). NOT a mechanism change and NOT a re-derivation of any measured-behaviour parameter (rule 23 untouched: no guard, constant, or detector default moved) — a reproducibility fix that makes a committed measured artifact byte-reproduce from its own frozen generator + committed source data, the caiso-78/nyiso-62/neiso-59 re-gate family (rule 14/15: the corrected extract is strictly more accurate measured availability truth; keeping the stale file would bury real outages inside phantom capacity). LOYO (rule 22): exempt by the same precedent — a year-invariant input regeneration with zero fitted parameters (the windows are each unit's own CEMS record; coverage rises comparably in all three years, not selectively in the studied one). ZERO-FORCING ABLATION TWIN of 2026-07-14-miso-65-outage-regen (rule 20): merchant floors off — including st_gas_mustrun_per_plant (MECH_ABLATION_FIELDS) — structural mechanisms kept: the topology split, RDT TCDC + RPE violation pricing, the committed take-or-pay / warm-boiler offer pricing, the outage overlays (incl. the short-window channel and the regenerated >= 5-day extract) and the class-aware fuel-price donor are offer structure / pricing / availability inputs, not floors, and stay armed.
